assumptions: Adjacent fragments share enough terminal homology to anneal and extend.
limits: Does not model mispriming, the polymerase or cycling; the overlap rule is sequence identity.
bio.jane/contract.question: What single product does overlap-extension PCR give from fragments that share terminal homology?

description: Overlap-extension (fusion) PCR — join fragments that share terminal homology into one product, carrying their features across (pydna). Emits the fused product as a NEW record.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

fragments.description: the fragments to fuse, in order — wire upstream `record` outputs here, or name library documents.

include_subject.description: also include the node's subject as the first fragment.

limit.description: minimum shared terminal homology two fragments must have to fuse (pydna's own default is 15). In bp.

name: fusion_pcr

junctions.description: the first product's joins: each overlap's product coordinates (0-based inclusive), bases, length and Tm

productTm.description: product melting temperature of the first product

record.description: the fused product, as a record
